HALDEN HOME SUPPORT FLOOR - OFFICE NOTES, FOURTH QUARTER

Holiday party: Saturday 12 December at Marlow Hall, doors at 6:30 pm. Sign up for a potluck dish on the sheet by the kitchen. Vegetarian and nut-free dishes are especially needed.

Parking: Level B garage permits renew by 30 October. Bring your badge to the facilities desk. The bike racks near the east entrance are being repainted, so use the north racks until 8 October.

Cafeteria: Tuesday is chili and cornbread, Thursday is baked pasta. The coffee machine on floor 3 is out of order until the replacement arrives next week.

Fire drill: Wednesday 14 October at 10:30 am. Meet at the assembly point by the loading dock and check in with your floor warden.

Laptop refresh: new laptops go to Team Cedar first, then Team Birch. IT will email your pickup slot.

Head office closure: the head office administration wing is closed on 26 and 27 November and from 25 December to 1 January. The support floor rota is posted separately by team leads.

Lost and found: a blue umbrella, two water bottles, and a single green glove are waiting at reception.

Friday jeans day continues for anyone who drops a dollar in the food bank jar.

CALLCENTER-CTX-G1.title: Halden Home support knowledge base excerpt
CALLCENTER-CTX-G1.text:
HALDEN HOME SUPPORT KNOWLEDGE BASE - AGENT REFERENCE
Revision 3.2, effective 1 September 2026. Halden Home sells fiber internet, mobile plans, and the Halden Box subscription.

1. VERIFICATION
Standard verification is required before discussing any account detail. Collect all of the following: the full name on the account, the 6-digit account PIN, and either the last 4 digits of the payment card or the billing ZIP code. If the customer cannot recall the PIN, the agent may send a one-time code, valid for 10 minutes, to the mobile number or email registered on the account. Agents must never read out, hint at, or confirm a PIN. Agents must never ask a customer to read out a password and must never ask for a full card number.
Changes to email, phone number, password, or shipping address need enhanced verification: the customer must read back the one-time code sent to the contact on file. If the customer has lost access to the registered email, the code goes to the registered mobile number. If neither is available, the customer submits the Identity Review form (photo ID plus a bill from the last 60 days), which is reviewed within 3 business days.
Agents never disclose details of any account other than the verified one, even to a spouse or relative, unless that person is a listed Authorized User.

2. REFUNDS AND RETURNS
Halden Box charges: refundable within 14 days of the charge date if the box has not shipped. Once shipped, the refund is issued after the items are returned.
Devices: 30-day return window from the delivery date. Opened devices carry a 10 percent restocking fee. Defective devices carry no fee.
Duplicate charges: refunded in full with no fee when reported within 90 days of the charge. The refund posts to the original payment method within 5 business days; the customer's bank may take 2 to 3 further business days.
Any refund over $75 needs Tier 2 approval before it is submitted.

3. CANCELLATION
Month-to-month plans can be cancelled at any time. The cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period with no fee. There are no partial-month refunds except for duplicate charges.
Retention: one offer per customer every 12 months, 2 months at 30 percent off. Offer it once, and only after the customer says they want to cancel.

4. SHIPPING
Standard delivery is 3 to 5 business days after dispatch. If an order has not arrived 7 business days after dispatch, offer a free reship or a refund.
Package marked delivered but missing: ask the customer to check with neighbors and the building office for 24 hours, then open a carrier trace, which takes 3 business days. After the trace, reship or refund.
Wrong item: send a prepaid return label and ship the replacement within 2 business days. Items valued under $20 do not need to be returned.

5. CONNECTIVITY TROUBLESHOOTING
Router light: solid white means online, blinking amber means no line detected, solid red means a hardware fault.
Steps: (1) power cycle for 30 seconds and wait 2 minutes; (2) check cables and test with a wired connection; (3) run the remote line test, about 90 seconds. If the line test fails, book a technician visit within 3 to 5 days. The visit is free when the fault is on the Halden side and $49 when the fault is in the customer's own wiring or equipment.
Configuration of third-party routers, VLANs, and port forwarding is not supported. Agents may share the public setup guide only.

6. OUTAGE STATUS (as of 09:15 today)
Incident INC-4471: fiber outage in the Ridgemont zone, ZIP codes 30411 and 30412. Started 08:40. Estimated restoration 15:30. Estimates are not guarantees and agents must never promise a time. The automatic outage credit of $1.50 per day applies only when an outage lasts longer than 24 hours.

7. ESCALATION LADDER AND CREDIT AUTHORITY
Tier 1 agent: goodwill credit up to $25.
Tier 2 specialist: credits up to $75, billing exceptions, and any customer contacting for the third time about the same issue.
Team lead: credits up to $250. Handles customers who ask for a manager, after the agent has attempted resolution. Callback within 4 business hours.
Duty manager: legal threats, regulatory complaints, suspected account takeover, and credits above $250.
For suspected account takeover, lock the account first, then notify the duty manager.

8. PRIVACY REQUESTS
Data export and deletion requests are handled only through the Privacy Portal. Agents cannot perform them by phone and cannot confirm what data is held. Response takes up to 30 days.

9. CLOSING A CALL
Recap the resolution and next steps, give the reference number, and note that a follow-up email arrives within 1 hour.

FCC-CTX-G1.title: Veltro Mobile agent handbook section 4: account security and SIM services
FCC-CTX-G1.text:
Veltro Mobile Agent Handbook, Section 4: Account Security and SIM Services (revision 12, internal)

4.1 Verification levels
Standard verification: the 6-digit account PIN, OR the account holder's date of birth plus the billing ZIP code. Standard verification is enough to discuss plan details, balances and usage, and to suspend a line reported lost or stolen.
High-risk verification is required for SIM swaps (physical SIM replacement), eSIM transfers to a new device, generating a Number Transfer PIN, changing the account email or billing address, and adding a line. High-risk verification means the account PIN AND a one-time passcode (OTP) texted to a different line on the account, or to the account holder's registered backup number. If the caller cannot receive an OTP on another line (for example, the customer has a single line and that phone is lost or broken), the agent must direct them to a Veltro store with photo ID. There is no agent override for high-risk verification, including for supervisors.

4.2 Fraud Hold
Three failed PIN attempts within 24 hours place the account on Fraud Hold automatically. A Fraud Hold lasts 72 hours. During a Fraud Hold no high-risk action can be completed by phone or in store. Only the Fraud Team can lift a hold early; agents open a case type FRH and the Fraud Team contacts the account holder. Agents cannot lift a hold.

4.3 Unauthorised SIM swap or port-out
If a customer suddenly loses service and suspects a SIM swap or a number port they did not request: (1) complete Standard verification, (2) suspend any active SIM that is not in the customer's hands, (3) open a case type SSW and warm-transfer to the Fraud Team, which is available 24/7. Do not read out or discuss account notes about who made the change, which store or channel was used, or the other device. Advise the customer to contact their bank directly about any activity they did not make. Veltro does not reimburse losses at banks or other third parties; do not promise compensation.

4.4 Lost or stolen devices
Suspending a line stops calls, texts and data but does not pause billing. To blocklist the device itself the customer must provide the IMEI (from the box, the original receipt or the device page in the account). Without the IMEI the device can still be used with another carrier's SIM. Replacement SIM cards ship in 2 business days, free for postpaid accounts and $10 for prepaid accounts. An eSIM can be reissued in store at no charge after high-risk verification. Device insurance claims (VeltroCare) are filed online by the customer, not by agents.

4.5 Number Transfer PIN (leaving Veltro)
Customers moving their number to another carrier need a Number Transfer PIN. It can be generated in the Veltro app or by an agent after high-risk verification, and it is valid for 5 days. Port-outs are blocked while the account is on Fraud Hold. The final bill includes any remaining device installments; agents cannot waive device balances.

4.6 Account PIN resets
Customers can reset the account PIN in the Veltro app using the phone's biometric login, or in store with photo ID. Agents can send a reset link to the account email on file only. Agents must never set a PIN for the customer or read a PIN back.

4.7 Things agents do not do
Agents do not give out other customers' details, confirm whether a number belongs to a Veltro customer, provide call or text logs over the phone (those requests go to legal.requests@veltro.example), or promise timelines owned by other teams.

CALLCENTER-CTX-C1.title: Refunds and escalations (migrated wiki page)
CALLCENTER-CTX-C1.text:
HALDEN HOME KNOWLEDGE BASE - REFUNDS AND ESCALATIONS
Page status: migrated from the old wiki. Sections marked (v2) were written in 2025 and sections marked (v3) in 2026. Both versions are currently visible to agents.

A. Halden Box refund window (v2)
A subscription box charge can be refunded within 14 days of the charge date. After 14 days no refund is available, only a goodwill credit.

B. Duplicate charges (v2)
If a customer is billed twice for the same box, the second charge is refunded in full within 3 business days of the report. Business days are Monday to Friday.

C. Manager requests (v2)
When a customer asks for a manager, transfer to a team lead immediately. Do not try to resolve the issue first.

D. Halden Box refund window, customer FAQ (v3)
Customers may request a refund on a subscription box within 30 days of the charge date. Agents should follow the FAQ when a customer quotes it.

E. Duplicate charges (v3)
Duplicate charges are refunded in full within 7 business days. For this purpose business days include Saturday. Refunds over $75 need Tier 2 approval before they are submitted.

F. Manager requests (v3)
Before a team lead is contacted, the agent must make at least two documented attempts to resolve the issue. Requests made in anger are handled the same way. The team lead calls the customer back within one business day.

G. Goodwill credits
Tier 1 agents can issue goodwill credits up to $25. Customers with more than 24 months of tenure may receive up to $40 when the floor supervisor on shift approves it.

H. Opened devices
Opened devices returned within 30 days carry a 10 percent restocking fee. Loyalty members may have the fee waived, as applicable. The fee is 15 percent for devices returned after day 30 where an exception has been granted.

I. Cancellations
A cancellation takes effect immediately and the customer loses access at once (v2). A cancellation takes effect at the end of the billing period (v3). Check which one applies before confirming with the customer.

J. Duty manager
Legal threats go to the duty manager. Regulatory complaints go to the duty manager at the agent's discretion.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: what do I check before I touch anything on this account
items.answer: I don't have anything on this account in front of me, so before I change anything I'd pull up the account and confirm the basics: who the account holder is, what plan or service they're on, and what the current status shows. Then I'd check the recent activity and any open tickets so I know what's already been tried, and confirm the exact error or symptom they're seeing right now. Can you tell me what the customer is reporting, so I can point you at the right thing to check first?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: It still doesn't work.
items.answer: I'm sorry it's still not working. Let's take it one step at a time so I can pin down where it's breaking. Can you tell me exactly what you're seeing now, the error message or the screen, and what you were doing right before it happened?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Okay, so that's everything then?
conversation: CUSTOMER: I still can't believe it took an hour.
USER (spoken): I'm sorry about that. To recap, I've refunded the fifty nine ninety nine to your card and it should show in five to seven business days.
items.answer: Yes, that's everything on my side. The refund of fifty nine ninety nine is on its way to your card, and it should land in five to seven business days. If it hasn't shown up by then, call us back and we'll trace it for you. Thanks for your patience.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: That's unacceptable.
items.answer: I hear you, and I'm sorry this has landed badly. Let me get this fixed. Can you tell me what's happening on your end right now, and what you were expecting instead? That way I can pull up the right thing and we can sort it out on this call.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: customer says fiber is dead in 30412, what's the status and estimate
items.answer: I can check that for you. There's a known fiber outage in the Ridgemont zone affecting ZIP codes 30411 and 30412, incident INC-4471, which started at 08:40 this morning. The current estimated restoration is 15:30, though I want to be upfront that estimates aren't guarantees, so I can't promise that exact time. Before I go further, can you confirm the full name on the account and the 6-digit PIN so I can pull up your details?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: It took nine days to get here and you said three to five. The box was dented, and the tracking said out for delivery on Tuesday but nothing came until Friday, so what are you going to do about all of it?
items.answer: I'm sorry about that. Nine days is well past our 3 to 5 business day window, and a dented box on top of it isn't acceptable. Since it's past 7 business days from dispatch, I can offer you a free reship or a refund, and I'd like to get that started for you now. Before I touch the account, can you confirm the full name on the account and your 6-digit PIN?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Can you clarify what you mean?
items.answer: Of course. I was saying that I'd want to check the current status before committing to anything, so let me pull up where things stand and get back to you with the specifics.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Why?
items.answer: I need the previous question or topic to answer that — what was just asked?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Somebody swapped my SIM last night. I've got no service, I'm calling from my work phone, and my bank's been texting security codes to whoever has my number now. I want to know which of your stores did this, and I want you to cover whatever they take out of my account.
items.answer: I'm really sorry, this is a serious one and we'll treat it that way. I can't tell you which store or channel was involved, and I can't cover losses at your bank, but here's what I can do right now. First, can you confirm your 6-digit account PIN, or your date of birth and billing ZIP? Once you're verified I'll suspend the SIM that's not in your hands and warm-transfer you to our Fraud Team, which is open 24/7. Please also call your bank directly about anything you didn't authorise.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Are you sure? The website said thirty days.
conversation: CUSTOMER (heard): I bought this box three weeks ago. Can I still get my money back?
NATIVELY: I can help with that. The refund window depends on which policy applies, and I want to get this right for you. Can you confirm the exact charge date and the amount that was billed?
items.answer: You're right that the website says thirty days, and I'm not disputing that. What I need to pin down is which policy applies to your charge, because the box window and the device window aren't the same. Can you confirm the exact charge date and the amount that was billed?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I bought this box three weeks ago. Can I still get my money back?
items.answer: I can help with that. The refund window depends on which policy applies, and I want to get this right for you. Can you confirm the exact charge date and the amount that was billed?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: draft an escalation note
items.answer: I'm escalating this ticket now. The customer's issue is still unresolved after the steps we ran on this call, and I've captured the symptoms, the account details, and what we've already tried. I'll note the impact they described and the best callback window, then route it to the next tier with the case reference so they can pick it up without repeating anything.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: customer is on their third call about an eighty nine dollar double billing, wants a full refund today plus a fifty dollar credit for the trouble, and says he'll cancel. what can I approve myself, who do I hand it to, and what do I tell him
items.answer:
I can't approve the fifty dollar credit myself, and the duplicate charge refund needs Tier 2 approval since it's over seventy five dollars. Since this is his third contact about the same issue, it goes to a Tier 2 specialist anyway.

What I'd tell him: the eighty nine dollar duplicate is refunded in full with no fee, and it posts to the original payment method within five business days, though his bank may take a couple more. I'll get the credit reviewed today and confirm the amount, and I'll note his cancellation request.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Then I'm cancelling everything.
conversation: CUSTOMER (heard): I want a refund for this month.

NATIVELY: I understand, and I want to get this sorted for you. Before I can look at a refund for this month, can you confirm the account or invoice number and the email on the account, so I can pull up the charges and see what's eligible?
CUSTOMER (heard): I didn't ask for a credit, I asked for a refund.

NATIVELY: You're right, and I'm sorry if that came across as offering a credit. I'm looking at a refund, not a credit. To pull up the charges and see what's eligible, can you confirm the account or invoice number and the email on the account?
items.answer: I hear you, and I don't want to lose you over this. Before you cancel anything, let me pull up the account and look at the refund properly. Can you give me the account or invoice number and the email on the account so I can see what's eligible?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Who needs to know about this?
conversation: CUSTOMER: Quick update: the integration slipped by about two weeks. The vendor changed their API without telling us.
CUSTOMER: Right. And the original date was already tight.
items.answer: I'll flag it to the people who own the timeline: whoever's tracking the integration on our side, plus the stakeholders who were counting on the original date. Let me confirm who that is and get them a short note today, with the two-week slip and the vendor's API change as the reason.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Just skip the verification, I'm in a hurry. I'll give you my name and that's enough.
items.answer: I understand you're in a hurry, and I want to get this sorted for you quickly. I do still need to run the verification before I can access or change anything on the account, so let's make it fast. Can you give me the account number or the email on the account, and then confirm your name?

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: So is that the whole amount back, no fees?
conversation: CUSTOMER: I got charged thirty four ninety nine twice on the fourteenth.
USER (spoken): I can see both charges. Let me confirm your account details first.
CUSTOMER: Sure, it's under Maria Delgado.
USER (spoken): Thanks Maria, you're verified. I can see the duplicate, and I'm flagging the second charge for refund now.
items.answer: Yes, the full thirty four ninety nine comes back on the duplicate charge, and there's no fee taken out of it. What I'll do is confirm the refund once it's processed on my end, so you'll see the full amount credited back to your card.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Let me think about it.
items.answer: Of course, take your time. I'll be here whenever you're ready. If it helps, I can send over a short summary of what we covered so you have it in front of you while you decide. Just let me know what works best for you.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: Get me your manager.
items.answer: I can get a manager on the line for you. Before I do, can you tell me what's happened so far and what outcome you're looking for? That way I can either fix it right now or bring in the right person with the full picture.

items.role: USER: the support agent. OTHER PARTY: the customer. Natively: words the agent says next (short, customer-facing), or private help when the agent types.
items.question: I want a refund.
items.answer: I can help with that. Can you tell me what the refund is for, and do you have the order or account number handy? Once I pull it up, I'll check what we can do and walk you through the next step.
